transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hey. Yeah, um... so I guess I came in because ever since my sister and her baby moved back home, I’ve just been way more on edge. And kind of down than usual, too. I keep snapping over just stupid little stuff at the house, and then I show up to class or the shop already completely drained. 

I work on industrial machinery, like refractory stuff, which is usually great. Like, last week we were working on this massive rotary kiln and the bearings were completely shot—grease everywhere, took us literally half the shift just to get the casing off. I actually really like getting my hands dirty like that, it's way better than sitting at a desk all day. My dad always said I had a knack for it since I was like, ten, when I took apart the lawnmower... but anyway, what was I saying? 

Right, so with work and school, I'm still getting by, mostly, but I’ve missed a couple of deadlines lately. I even had to back out of helping build the set for the theater department. Which sucks, because I usually do all their heavy rigging. The rigging we did for the spring show was awesome, we used this whole counterweight system with pulleys that I welded myself... but yeah, I just couldn't keep everything straight in my head right now with the baby crying and everything else, so I had to drop the theater stuff.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much enjoyment out of things you usually like, like working on machinery or helping with the theater set?

Um, I don't know if it's that I'm not enjoying it. I still like the work. It's just... I'm so tired before I even get there. Like yesterday, we had this massive conveyor belt system that got jammed up at the recycling plant, and usually, I'd be all over that. It's cool figuring out where the tension is off, you know? You have to recalibrate the rollers, and sometimes the whole alignment is just shot because someone didn't grease the bearings right. I always tell the new guys, you have to pack the grease in there, not just smear it on the outside. It's like when you're changing the oil on a car, you don't just pour it over the engine block. My buddy Dave did that once in high school, ruined his dad's truck... but yeah, I don't think I've stopped liking the stuff I do. I just haven't had the energy to get into it the same way.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you felt down or low most of the day, nearly every day?

Um, not most of the day, no. I mean, I definitely feel bummed out sometimes, mostly when I'm stuck at the house and the baby is just screaming. But it's not like an all-day thing. Usually, once I get out and get to the shop, I'm alright. 

Actually, my boss just bought this brand new CNC plasma cutter for the shop, and it is insane. It cuts through half-inch steel plate like it's literal butter. We spent like three hours on Tuesday just programming it to cut out these custom brackets for a suspension lift. My buddy Tyler has this old Tacoma he's been trying to lift for months, but the aftermarket kits are way too expensive, so we figured we'd just fabricate the parts ourselves. The only problem is getting the tolerance right, because if you're off by even a fraction of an inch on the control arms, the whole alignment is completely screwed up and it drives like a boat... so you really have to dial in the CAD software first before you even fire up the torch. 

But, uh... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling down. Yeah, no, not all day every day. Just mostly when I'm at home dealing with the noise.

Psychotic or organic disorders (F06.3) were not supported by the history.
